after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
The matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 0 \\ 0 & b\end{aligned}]
$$

represents the linear transformation that acts on a vector in ${R}^{2}$ as follows (in the order given):

- It rotates the vector  $\pi $ radians counterclockwise about the origin, then

- stretches the result by a scale factor of $3$ parallel to the $x$-axis, and finally

- reflects the result about the $x$-axis.

What is the value of $a+b?$
after.worked_solution:
Let $P$ be the matrix that represents the rotation, $Q$ be the matrix that represents the stretching, and $R$ be the matrix that represents the reflection. These are given by the following elementary transformation matrices:

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}],\,Q=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,R=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Hence, the combined transformation can be represented by the matrix $RQP:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RQP & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,
$a+b=(-3)+1=-2.$
